summary: Skorobogatov and Sofos prove Schinzel's Hypothesis (H) for 100% of n-tuples of integer polynomials of fixed degrees ordered by height: an averaged Bateman–Horn estimate (Theorem 1.9) by Linnik's dispersion method, with two-point prime correlations over coefficient boxes from Davenport's Möbius cancellation (§3) and local densities from a Bernoulli model (§2). They deduce density-one Hasse principles for cyclic norm equations N(z) = P(t) and diagonal conic bundles, and a 56% lower bound for x² + y² = f(t) (§§5–7). 103 items (6 library, 6 planned, 91 missing) are routed to two proposed Part IIs (Schinzel averages; random fibrations) and to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0, AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2/AN.5, ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.0, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2/SV.4 and HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.2. Twenty-two findings are recorded. The main one: Lemma 3.14 is false for positive primes (E1), and the von Mangoldt function must be even on ℤ (E4); the proofs establish the both-sign forms, and the main theorems survive through the von Mangoldt count and a bound on negative values that uses A₁ > n.
